svg.aria-label: A grid of 13 models against 10 countries showing what a month of moderate use costs as a share of monthly income. The cheapest model on the grid costs 4.6% of monthly income and the dearest 268%, so affordability turns on which model a user picks, not only on where they live. Across the countries with a statutory minimum wage, a month of moderate use costs between 4 and 1,899 hours of minimum-wage work.
svg.text: A month of moderate use, as a share of monthly income
20 x the standard workload (1M input + 250k output tokens), against GNI per capita, Atlas method, divided by 12. Built on the record's frozen unit, unchanged since the first release.
Cells show the share of monthly GNI per capita; above 100% means a month of use costs more than a month of average income. Minimum-wage hours are in the data table.
Data: the Observatory record · CC BY 4.0 · compiled 2026-09-23 · income base is the Atlas method, which smooths exchange rates
